item.content:encoded:
This is no doubt echoing prior comments, but this this entry feels really dated. The excessive use of redactions, expungements, and a whole lot of other vagueness where more story could be all work together to make the piece feel clunky. While I think the initial hook is strong enough, there isn't enough substance to the rest of it. -1

Show More
Hide Text

I like the premise. The idea of a giant tunnel system made out of fossilized tissue is really cool, because of all that it could imply. Further, I think that the images used on the entry add a lot to the mysterious atmosphere of the piece. Though I did notice as I went through it that the images were all in different styles, like how the first one used color and the second two are in black and white, which isn't a huge issue, it did briefly take me out of it.

If I were to point to anywhere to flesh this out, I'd add more exploration logs or, if you want to keep those vague, I would add in various containment proposals like it mentions in the piece's description. That could serve to give us a better idea of what the heck is going on down there without spelling it out.

Lastly, and this is more of a small point, but under Addendum 238-S7, you wrote "Further research into SCP-238 will be carried out by Dr. ████ and his research staff, under SCP supervision." which sounds strange. I assume he's this means that he's being supervised by the Foundation, but unless he's being hired as a subcontractor by them, wouldn't this doctor be considered the Foundation's supervisor here? I'd change that from "SCP supervision" to the supervision of some high level person.

item.content:encoded:
This one's age is showing. Not so much in its tone or expungement use, though those could stand to be tuned up, but in its inexpert use of a lot of tropes that have since become site staples. It lacks any particular character. A huge underground facility is mentioned, but not elaborated upon. It's biological and there's rotting flesh in it, but we don't know what kinds or what they're doing. It causes hallucinations, but there's no mention of hallucinations. And the exploration log doesn't really describe any actual events.

I can't really blame it for that cuz merely including all these elements in one place was probably pretty solid back in the day, but everything done here was done much better in some other exploration-focused piece later.

Does "noises" have to be put in quotation marks? If its quoting a persons deception of it maybe put more then just a single word from their account of the contents of the exploration they must have embarked on to get said account.
Lets go with the scenario that, regardless of whether or not the person survived the experience with 238 they simply stated "I hear noises", realistically speaking there is no way the quote would have ended at that unless this was their final words. The people outside listening in; who by the pages admissions are able to keep track of the agents life signs, are also able to say things to the agents; as is rather standard, somebody outside is bound to say "what kind of noises".

Since this article includes a black-boxed scip, I'd like to work in a link to SCP-1013, another article by Dr. Gears. This is in part due to the juvenile instances of SCP-1013 actively seeking out cool and dark places to rapidly grow until they reach "adult size". At which point, they will attempt to establish a territory which has worse implications given that SCP-238 is an infinitely large sewer system.

Additionally, since vision would be limited in a dark and enclosed space like SCP-238, introducing something to it that requires direct eye contact be made in order to trigger its mode of function would present a new challenge. Within SCP-1013's article there are also implications that it has escaped before, albeit with different results other than it being re-contained. Of note, while there are a few scips that populate areas such as sewer systems, these were all within Series I, so ideally linking this to a Series II or III article would be better.

Editing this passage:

Upon escape of SCP-███, the local SCP Team assigned to SCP-238 reported SCP-███ breaking through the original wall and entering the underground chambers. After O5-█, O5-█, O5-█, Dr. ██████, and Dr. ██████████ were notified, they elected to send in a single team to retrieve SCP-███. Further information regarding the expedition is found in document 238-S7-A, with clearance level three (3) required. The end result of the retrieval team were six dead, two critically injured, one missing in action, and SCP-███ re-captured. Further research into SCP-238 will be carried out by Dr. ████ and his research staff, under SCP supervision.

To read:

Upon the escape of six juvenile instances of SCP-1013, the local SCP Team assigned to SCP-238 reported SCP-1013 squeezing through the original wall and entering the underground chambers. After O5-█, O5-█, O5-█, Dr. ██████, and Dr. ██████████ were notified, they elected to send in a single team to retrieve SCP-1013. Further information regarding the expedition is found in document 238-S7-A, with clearance level three (3) required. The end result of the retrieval team were six dead, two critically injured, one missing in action, and the six juvenile SCP-1013 instances being re-captured. Further research into SCP-238 will be carried out by Dr. ████ and his research staff, under SCP supervision.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.content:encoded:
I really like the idea of this. There there seem to be a few "labyrinth" type SCPs, but from what I've read so far most are extradimensional, or magical in some way.

Not this one. This one is just huge. They already know it has thousands of kilometers of tunnels, and that could just be the tip of the iceberg. I just love the scale of it and the fact that there could be anything down there.

But… There just doesn't seem to be much in the article that's actually interesting or creepy enough. Yes it's huge, and I'm curious about it enough to want to know more, but in the article there's nothing to really show why it's an SCP. Why is it Keter, especially since it seems you can just wall it off and forget about it?

There's one thing that did pique my interest:

Upon escape of SCP-███, the local SCP Team assigned to SCP-238 reported SCP-███ breaking through the original wall and entering the underground chambers.

I can't see the foundation storing an active and mobile SCP right outside SCP-238, so what made the escaped SCP-███ go down there? Is there something down there "calling" SCPs to itself? I think that would need to be expanded on though.

So… Not enough there for me to upvote, but enough good threads that I wouldn't downvote either. I hope more gets done with this sometime. Is it in any Tales?

item.content:encoded: I actually really liked this article. I'm imagining a scientific community, similar in purpose and style as the Foundation, except much larger and far older. This place housed hundreds, maybe thousands of SCPs within its sprawling facility. After some time, a localized event occurred that ended up crippling and destroying the entire facility, maybe pushing them into an emergency lock down so that nothing would escape. As the scientists and personnel locked within started going crazy, dying from hunger/thirst, or were killed off by unknown means, SCPs containment grew more and more lax. Eventually, escapes were commonplace, and a tiny "ecosystem" of SCPs developed in this massive underground world. Some SCPs were destroyed, some prospered, and some just disappeared. What's left in there are the strongest, most obscure, and hardest to contain SCPs. Undoubtedly, one of those SCPs is what killed the two agents.
